text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed in quiet dealings. March added $0.20 to close at $298.30 per tonne, while May gave up $0.10 to close at $297.60 per tonne. Hopes that lower prices will lead to higher physical demand have so far not materialized.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed a see-saw session lower. March lost 8 points to close at 10.33 cents/lb, while May gave up 5 points to close at 10.38 cents/lb. In spite of bearish fundamentals some players expect prices to rise because funds are heavily short and will look to cover positions.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 14,313 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 13,953 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1996 (January/December) up to 188,832 tonnes against 173,712 tonnes in 1995 and 192,368 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/December 1996 were Denmark with 107,075 tonnes whites against 114,014 tonnes, the United Kingdom with 43,950 tonnes, up from 38,734 tonnes, and Sweden with 11,894 tonnes compared to 142 tonnes.

DENMARK - Sugar exports in October 1996, the first month of the 1996/97 campaign (October/September), reached 12,578 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 18,342 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 172,938 tonnes against 199,559 tonnes in 1994/95 and 255,177 tonnes in 1993/94. The major country of destination October 1996 was Norway with 9,651 tonnes, down from 12,084 tonnes in October 1995.

Denmark will have a much greater export availability in 1996/97 after production rose to 547,000 tonnes compared to 470,000 tonnes in 1995/96. Sugar imports in October 1996 amounted to 5,871 tonnes, up from 1,062 tonnes in October 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 29,365 tonnes compared to 4,960 tonnes in 1994/95. The country imports most of its sugar from Germany.

The European Union awarded 14,250 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 45.422 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to January 29 reached 1,396,600 tonnes, which compares to 1,560,248 tonnes last year.
